label: input token y at original positions 0-3
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is y during the first four original-phase steps (t = 0..3), on every such occurrence (precision 1.0, recall ~1.0). Magnitude depends on position: strongest at t = 1 (~1.0 of max) and t = 2 (~0.94), about 0.75 at t = 0, and weak at t = 3 (~0.26-0.31 relative). It does not depend on L, the previous token, or whether y repeats; a second y right after the first still fires near full strength. It does not fire on y at original positions >= 4, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (except a few negligible traces, around 0.02-0.14, when y is fed back as a copy-phase input).

issues: Test split scores reproduce: precision 1.000, recall 0.9992, F1 0.9996, mass recall 0.99994, with 0 false positives.

All 50 test misses are copy-phase steps where y is fed back as input (for example 'b y g <DEL> b [y:0.05]'), at 0.02-0.09 of max. They hold about 0% of activation mass, which matches the stated exception. The copy-phase traces form one systematic class, but it is negligible in mass.

Dev profile supports the position claims. It never fires at orig_idx >= 4, on the delimiter, or on any token other than y. Activation mass by t is 0.255 / 0.330 / 0.309 / 0.106 for t=0..3. Example magnitudes are about 0.75 at t=0, 1.00 at t=1, 0.94 at t=2 and 0.26-0.31 at t=3. Repeated y still fires ('i y y': 1.00 then 0.94).

Minor overclaim: the explanation says the feature does not depend on the previous token. Every top-activating example at max (1.00) has prev_tok = i, so the previous token probably shifts the magnitude slightly. Firing rate does not depend on it.
